name: What are the biggest cost overruns in ground-up construction?

mainEntity.name: What usually causes budget overruns on ground-up custom home projects in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What usually causes budget overruns on ground-up custom home projects in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most ground-up budget overruns come from a few predictable sources. Site surprises are a major one, especially on older, sloped, or heavily improved lots where soils, drainage, utilities, or access are not fully understood at the start. Another common cause is design changes after pricing, which can trigger rework, new materials, and schedule delays. Long-lead items such as windows, cabinetry, stone, and specialty fixtures also create risk if they are not ordered early. On custom homes, scope creep can become expensive when the project evolves during construction and the original budget no longer matches the final design. The safest way to control overruns is to complete early due diligence, keep selections organized, include contingency, and make sure the bid scope is detailed enough to compare apples to apples.
acceptedAnswer.description: The biggest overruns usually come from site surprises, design changes, permit delays, long-lead materials, and upgrades chosen after the budget is set. Hillside grading, soil issues, utility work, and structural changes can add major cost quickly. Late finish selections and scope creep are also common reasons budgets grow during construction.
